diagnostic_evidence.quote: with probability $1-3\delta$,  we have for $m\approx  S\log(S/\delta)$ that

issues.failure_explanation: The only proved bound is (Cn/S)·sum_{i>S} lambda_i with m ≈ S log(S/δ), i.e. S ≈ m/log m. Combined with Gaussian-kernel eigenvalue decay this gives decay like exp(-c (m/log m)^{1/d}), which is strictly slower than the advertised O(m exp(-alpha m^{1/d})) for every fixed alpha>0.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restate the guarantee with the rate actually implied (roughly (n log m/m)·exp(-c (m/log m)^{1/d})), or prove a bound with sample complexity linear in S.
issues.overall_effect: The quantitative convergence rate promised in the Contribution subsection is not delivered by the paper's theorem; only a stretched-exponential rate is supported.
issues.title: Advertised compression rate is faster than the stated bound yields
issues.why_classification: The advertised rate must be weakened, but a recognizably comparable fast-decay guarantee survives with a local restatement; no new proof architecture is required.

issues.failure_explanation: The wedge product is alternating, so replacing an orthonormal basis of the tangent space by one related through a determinant -1 orthogonal map flips the sign of e_1∧…∧e_m. Hence τ^S (and likewise τ^{N_S}) is defined only up to sign, and the currents [S] and N(S) are not well defined unless an orientation is chosen (unoriented rectifiable sets give varifolds, not currents).

failure_location.quote: the choice of basis vectors does not matter due to invariance of wedge product under change of orthonomal basis.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Require oriented rectifiable sets / oriented normal bundles and state the orientation convention, or replace currents by varifold-type objects.
issues.overall_effect: The foundational definitions of [S] and N(S), and hence every subsequent normal-cycle identity, are ambiguous up to sign.
issues.title: Wedge product claimed invariant under all orthonormal basis changes
issues.why_classification: Adding the standard orientation datum is a short local fix that leaves all formulas, rates and guarantees intact up to consistent signs.
